title: Using generated item art in an auction game: what should the artwork tell the player?
author: CrownedGames
selftext:
We’re Crowned Games, developing Bid Rivals, a free-to-play multiplayer auction game. Some of its artwork uses pre-generated AI-assisted assets. This clip is captured gameplay, not generated video.



The interesting design problem is that an attractive item illustration can suggest value before the player has enough information. In this game, buying intel and placing bids both use Gold. The interface shows the information available for the decision; the artwork gives the items their appearance.



For developers using generated collectibles, how do you keep visual richness from becoming an accidental rarity signal? Would you make rarity explicit in the interface, constrain the artwork by tier, or let players learn the visual patterns? I’m especially interested in cases where a detailed-looking item should not automatically mean a better bid.



The 18-second clip cuts between intel, bid entry, reveal and collection screens. It is a feature montage, not one continuous auction. The game includes AI-assisted/generated art and audio.
